metadata.methods_description: EEG data were acquired at 1000 Hz sampling rate using a 32-channel ANT Neuro eego mylab amplifier with standard 10-05 electrode montage. Each trial consisted of a 500 ms fixation period, 500 ms cue presentation, and 5000 ms stimulus presentation. Participants attended to one of four overlapping SSVEP arrow stimuli flickering at frequencies of 14.17, 12.14, 9.44, and 7.73 Hz.

citation_details.title: Block Distributed Joint Temporal-Frequency- Phase Modulation for Steady-State Visual Evoked Potential Based Brain-Computer Interface With a Limited Number of Frequencies
citation_details.author: Sheng Ge, Hui Yang, Ruimin Wang, Yue Leng, Keiji Iramina, Pan Lin, Haixian Wang
citation_details.venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
citation_details.abstract: How to encode as many targets as possible with limited frequency resources is a grave problem that restricts the application of steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). In the current study, we propose a novel block-distributed joint temporal-frequency-phase modulation method for a virtual speller based on SSVEP-based BCI. A 48-target speller keyboard array is virtually divided into eight blocks and each block contains six targets. The coding cycle consists of two sessions: in the first session, each block flashes at different frequencies while all the targets in the same block flicker at the same frequency; in the second session, all the targets in the same block flash at different frequencies. Using this method, 48 targets can be coded with only eight frequencies, which greatly reduces the frequency resources required, and average accuracies of 86.81 $\pm$ 9.41% and 91.36 $\pm$ 6.41% were obtained for both the offline and online experiments

citation_details.author: Rui Li, D.-J. Bai, Zhijun Li, Shiqiang Yang, Weiping Liu, Yichi Zhang, Jincao Zhou, Jing Luo, Wen Wang
citation_details.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
citation_details.abstract: In recent years, the steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP) based brain control method has been employed to help people with disabilities because of its advantages of high information transmission rate and low training time. However, the existing SSVEP brain control methods cannot adapt to dynamic or unstructured environments. Moreover, the recognition accuracy from the conventional decoding algorithm still needs to improve. To address the above problems, this study proposed a steady-state hybrid visual evoked potentials (SSHVEP) paradigm using the grasping targets in their environment to improve the connection between the subjects' and their dynamic environments. citation_details.title: Application of Multi-Frequency Modular Distribution of Steady-State Visual Evoked Stimuli and Human-Computer Interaction
citation_details.author: Ziyu Ge
citation_details.venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
citation_details.abstract: In recent years, visual stimulation has received high attention in the research of brain-computer interface and human-computer interaction. Since SSVEP is not easily affected by human factors such as blinking and eye movement and myoelectric noise interference, it has been widely used in brain-computer interface system engineering. How to encode more visual stimuli with limited frequency and achieve BCI with high accuracy and transmission rate is the main problem in SSVEP-based brain computer interface system. In this study, I used a multi-frequency coding method with time and frequency interleaving to modularize the distribution of stimuli with similar frequencies to induce SSVEP signals in a shorter period of time, encode more stimulus modules with a small number of frequencies, and use canonical correlation analysis to explore the correlation between the original data and the comparison frequency, so as to produce command output with high accuracy.
